$comment: What kind of principal a DID names, read from the DID alone: a reader of the record does not know the knowledge base's domain, and a domain may hold colons. Split the DID on `:`. The last segment that is exactly `users` or `agents`, with at least one segment after it, is the kind segment: `agents` names software, `users` a person. A DID with no kind segment names a person, as it always has: the knowledge base's own DID, which seeds the vocabulary, is one. Everything after the kind segment is the principal's subject, which this rule does not read: an agent the gateway mints today has two segments there, its provider and its model, and a subject of one encoded segment reads the same way. Only the kind is read here.

absent.typescript: No TypeScript code reads a DID's kind: the record, in Rust, attributes every write, and the Browser reads the agents the record gives it.
absent.python: No Python code reads a DID's kind: the Librarian names people from the record's profiles, and the worker states its own generator.
absent.go: No Go code reads a DID's kind: the launcher and the Go SDK name the knowledge base and its people, and read no principal's DID.

cases.why: an agent named by its provider and model, as the gateway mints one today
an agent named by one encoded segment after `agents`, as an account's subject would be
a domain with a port: its colon is not a kind segment
a domain with a raw port colon, as a host:port domain is sometimes written
a domain whose path has a segment reading `users`: the last kind segment decides
a domain whose path has a segment reading `agents`: the last kind segment decides
`agents` with nothing after it is no kind segment
the knowledge base's own DID, which seeds the vocabulary, has no kind segment
an empty string names no one, and reads as a person
